newsitem.title: INDIA: India's STC denies report on Canada wheat quality.
newsitem.headline: India's STC denies report on Canada wheat quality.

text.p: The State Trading Corporation (STC) denied a newspaper report on Tuesday that India had contracted to buy poor quality wheat from Canada without checking for levels of poisonous mycotoxin.
"We are totally denying all the allegations. It is baseless," STC director Deepak Prasad told Reuters.
The Statesman newspaper said in a front-page report on Tuesday that quality standards and the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act had been compromised in wheat imports from Canada.

It said samples of Canadian wheat had failed a quality test conducted by the Indian Food Ministry, and the imports had been contracted with the Canadian Wheat Board without checking for levels of mycotoxin, a poisonous substance produced by a fungus.
A senior STC official said India would be getting the same quality of wheat it received from Canada in 1992.
"It will be certified by the Canadian Grain Commission so that it meets the 1992 import standards," he said.
He said India had contracted for 250,000 tonnes of imports from the Canadian Wheat Board and the first shipments were due in February.
